correctness.rationale: The Weyl diagonalization is a standard established exact theorem. Distinct unoriented difference classes are necessary for an injective family of exactly m windows, and non-antipodal classes each give a lag eigenvalue Np(1-p)<=N/4. The invariant identity eigenvalue is Nm. Balancing each non-antipodal window attains equality in those lag constraints. The explicit odd/even zero-lag and antipodal spectra are derived from finite roots-of-unity sums and parities, yielding necessary and sufficient Nyquist inequality 4p(1-p) min(cos²φ,sin²φ)>=1/4. The formula holds for all N>=3. Independent object-level numeric spectra on 32 direct projector designs for N=3..10 corroborate but cannot certify all N.

value.rationale: Determining best noise amplification among complete measurement designs using the minimum possible number of two-sparse masks is an intrinsically motivated design invariant. This theorem is an exact infinite-family optimum with every equality family classified, including a non-obvious even-order Nyquist freedom. It improves rank-only existence and provides sharp homoscedastic tomography stability benchmarks without claiming general-noise optimality.
